Fractured.description: A bone fracture is a complete or partial break in the bone, often caused by trauma, overuse, or conditions that weaken the bones such as osteoporosis. X-ray imaging reveals discontinuity in the bone structure.
symptoms: Acute pain at the fracture site
Swelling and bruising around the area
Deformity or abnormal positioning of limb
Difficulty bearing weight or moving the affected area
risk_factors: Age (children and elderly are more susceptible)
treatment: Surgical fixation (plates, screws, rods) for complex fractures
Pain management with NSAIDs or prescribed medications
prevention: Adequate calcium and vitamin D intake
Bone density screening for at-risk individuals

Not Fractured.description: The X-ray examination shows normal bone structure with no evidence of fracture, dislocation, or significant bony abnormality. The cortical margins are intact and the trabecular pattern is normal.
treatment: No treatment required for bone pathology
If symptoms persist, consider soft tissue evaluation (MRI/ultrasound)
Symptomatic treatment for any soft tissue pain
prevention: Maintain healthy bone density through diet and exercise

Glioma.description: Glioma is a type of brain tumor that originates from glial cells, which support and nourish neurons. Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors and can range from low-grade (slow-growing) to high-grade (aggressive, e.g., glioblastoma).
symptoms: Persistent headaches, often worse in the morning
risk_factors: Prior radiation therapy to the head
prevention: Regular neurological check-ups if at risk
Early detection through imaging if symptomatic

Meningioma.description: Meningioma is a tumor arising from the meninges, the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Most meningiomas are benign (WHO Grade I) and grow slowly, but some can be atypical or malignant.
causes: Abnormal growth of arachnoid cap cells
treatment: Observation with serial imaging for small asymptomatic tumors
Surgical excision for symptomatic or growing tumors
Stereotactic radiosurgery (Gamma Knife) for small tumors
Conventional radiation therapy for residual/recurrent tumors
prevention: Regular imaging follow-up if NF2 is present
Prompt evaluation of new neurological symptoms

No Tumor.description: The MRI examination shows normal brain parenchymal signal and structure. No abnormal masses, enhancement, or significant structural abnormality is detected. Ventricular size and sulcal pattern appear within normal limits.
treatment: No treatment required for brain pathology
Address presenting symptoms if any (e.g., headache management)
Consider alternative diagnoses if symptoms persist
prevention: Maintain overall brain health through exercise and diet
Avoid excessive alcohol and substance use

Pituitary.description: Pituitary tumor (adenoma) is a growth in the pituitary gland, a small gland at the base of the brain that controls hormone production. Most pituitary tumors are benign and can be functional (hormone-secreting) or non-functional.
causes: Abnormal cell proliferation in the anterior pituitary
Rarely associated with familial isolated pituitary adenoma
symptoms: Fatigue, weight changes, and mood disturbances
In women: menstrual irregularities; in men: erectile dysfunction
risk_factors: Family history of pituitary tumors or MEN1 syndrome
treatment: Medication (dopamine agonists for prolactinomas, somatostatin analogs)
Radiation therapy for residual or recurrent tumors
Hormone replacement therapy if pituitary function is impaired
prevention: Regular endocrine evaluation if at risk
Routine eye exams to detect visual field deficits early

Normal.description: The CT scan shows normal organ morphology and tissue density. No masses, fluid collections, or significant pathological findings are identified.

Lung Tumor.description: A mass or nodule detected in the lung parenchyma on CT imaging, which may represent primary lung cancer or metastatic disease. Further evaluation with biopsy and PET scan is typically recommended.
causes: Cigarette smoking (primary cause of lung cancer)
Exposure to radon gas, asbestos, or other carcinogens
Air pollution and secondhand smoke exposure
symptoms: Persistent cough that worsens over time
Chest pain, especially with deep breathing
prevention: Low-dose CT screening for high-risk individuals
Healthy diet rich in fruits and vegetables

Bone Fracture.description: CT imaging reveals a fracture — a break or crack in the bone. CT provides detailed cross-sectional views that can reveal complex fractures, fragments, and joint involvement not always visible on plain X-rays.
symptoms: Severe pain at the fracture site
Inability to bear weight or move the affected area
Numbness or tingling if nerves are involved
treatment: Surgical fixation for displaced or complex fractures
Bone stimulation therapy for non-union fractures
